abstract.text: We analyze the most general case of third-order Chern–Simons-like theories of massive 3D gravity. Results show the conditions for finding the unitary regions on the parameter space. There exists (n − 1)th order theories on the boundary of a unitary nth order model on parameter space under certain conditions, as the first example recently demonstrated from the bimetric generalization of exotic massive gravity. We investigated the mechanism that causes this type of transition for thirdorder models. Hamiltonian analysis of the theory also presents that ghost and no-ghost regions can be separated by Chern–Simons theories.

admission.original: We analyze the most general case of third-order Chern–Simons-like theories of massive 3D gravity. Results show the conditions for finding the unitary regions on the parameter space. There exists (n − 1)th order theories on the boundary of a unitary nth order model on parameter space under certain conditions, as the first example recently demonstrated from the bimetric generalization of exotic massive gravity. We investigated the mechanism that causes this type of transition for thirdorder models. Hamiltonian analysis of the theory also presents that ghost and no-ghost regions can be separated by Chern–Simons theories.

abstract.text: We analyze the most general case of third-order Chern–Simons-like theories of massive 3D gravity. Results show the conditions for finding the unitary regions on the parameter space. There exists (n − 1)th order theories on the boundary of a unitary nth order model on parameter space under certain conditions, as the first example recently demonstrated from the bimetric generalization of exotic massive gravity. We investigated the mechanism that causes this type of transition for thirdorder models. Hamiltonian analysis of the theory also presents that ghost and no-ghost regions can be separated by Chern–Simons theories.

citations.context: GR in three dimensions (3D) yields a trivial theory without any local degree of freedom [1].
However, a degree of freedom is attainable by adding a gravitational Chern–Simons term to an Einstein–Hilbert action in 3D, which is called topological massive gravity (TMG) [2].
Another example, new massive gravity (NMG) [3], is a parity-preserving fourth-order model and its linearization gives the Fierz–Pauli theory [4] with two massive graviton modes with helicity ±2.

If one abandons the parity-preserving condition on NMG the theory can be extended to general massive gravity (GMG) [5] that has ±2 helicity states with different masses and gives both TMG and NMG as a limit.

In the 3D case, the first-order formulation of the bimetric theory is known as zwei-dreibein gravity (ZDG) [8] that has a limiting case to NMG.
